Results.ReviewText: The Weber kettle grill has been around for decades, however I imagine not quite as built now.  The "kettle" part seems excellent, heavy and well coated, however the legs and wheels leave a bit to be desired.  If the legs were any thinner, you could use them as "tin foil".  The assembly with the push it lock buttons was convenient, but I own wrenches and would have preferred a more substantial fitment.  The features of the grill are nice, handle heat guards and the ash cleaner is great.  I'm happy with the purchase, but seriously doubt if I will be handing this down to my children or grandchildren as fathers did 50 years ago.
Results.Title: The same but different

Results.ReviewText: This grill is my third Weber grill.  My 1st one lasted 20 years!  It fell off of a truck and the handle broke off the lid.  It was riveted on, and could not be replaced.  The new design has a replaceable handle.  My 2nd was a Smokey Joe.  I could cook for 10 people by layering the food!  My new Weber conserves charcoal!  By closing the dampers, I can put out the fire and leave the coals til next time.  They stay dry even in torrential rain, and I just light them up the next time.  I get 4 to five uses out of each batch of charcoal!  I may add a few here and there, but the grill will pay for itself this first summer.  I love my Weber grill!
Results.Title: Here's to the Next 20 years of great grilling!

Results.ReviewText:
I couldn’t be happier with my new Original Kettle Charcoal Grill 22". This iconic grill lives up to its legendary reputation and then some. Assembly was quick and straightforward, with clear instructions and quality parts. Within an hour, I was ready to fire it up.

The design is timeless—sleek, sturdy, and compact enough for a small patio, yet spacious enough to grill for a group. The 22-inch cooking surface gives me plenty of room to handle everything from burgers and hot dogs to ribs and whole chickens.

What really stands out is how well it retains and distributes heat. The adjustable vents make temperature control a breeze, whether I’m going low and slow or searing steaks over high heat. The ash catcher system is also a game-changer—it makes cleanup fast and easy, which is a big plus.

Overall, the Original Kettle is a must-have for charcoal grill lovers. It’s affordable, durable, and delivers that unbeatable smoky flavor every time. Whether you're a grilling newbie or a seasoned BBQ pro, this grill is a fantastic choice!

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

Results.ReviewText: I bought my most recent Webber kettle grill to replace a 30 year old version. The old Webber had been moved across the country several times: spent winters outdoor in Ohio, lived in Nevada and Texas, in other words, my old grill owed me nothing at this point. I could have bought replacement parts but, sometimes you have to just hire the bullet and spend a little more. Speaking of price, my new grill cost me $30 more than my old grill. That’s a price increase of $1 per year; I can live with that. I have owned gas grills but I always go back to my charcoal fueled Webber kettle for taste and ease of use. Really, nothing beats a Webber kettle grill!

And now, with my newly purchased rotisserie, I’m taking my grilling game to legendary status. Juicy, slow-roasted meats? Yes, please! If you're on the fence about getting one—do it. This isn’t just a grill. It’s a lifestyle. 🔥🔥🔥

Results.ReviewText:
The Weber Original Kettle Premium 22" Charcoal Grill cooks well but is let down by a flimsy undercarriage. The kettle excels: it spreads heat evenly, with adjustable vents for precise temperature control (250°F-500°F). The porcelain-enameled grates are durable, and the One-Touch ash catcher makes cleanup simple.

However, the legs and wheels—thin aluminum and plastic—are too weak. Moving the grill requires caution; uneven surfaces or grass can jam the wheels, bending or collapsing the legs. The undercarriage’s poor quality doesn’t match the sturdy kettle, and the legs will likely fail first.

For the price tag, the grill’s legs should use thicker aluminum or steel for stability.  The kettle’s great, but the weak frame means I won’t buy again.

Handle it delicately—it’s fragile!
Results.Title: Poor Quality Undercarriage
